sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_27017c1f692149c79a16726ca19e8c2b
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>6</indicative_cases><key>itom-aiops-event</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>itom_health</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>ITOM Health: event management, AIOps and observability</name><overview>Ingest, reduce, bind, act. (1) Prefer OOB connectors (pull via MID) or the source tool's native push integration to the Event Management inbound endpoint; one integration per tool. (2) Event rules at the edge: ignore informational noise, normalise fields (node, type, resource, metric, message key), and set severity mapping. (3) CI binding by node name/IP/FQDN against a CMDB that follows the CMDB/CSDM pattern; unbound alerts are a data-quality signal, not an EM defect. (4) De-duplicate on message key, correlate with OOB tag-based and CMDB/service-based alert grouping (AIOps where licensed). (5) Alert management rules create incidents only for actionable, production, bound alerts, with service offering and support group from the CI; clearing policy agreed with the service desk. (6) Operator Workspace and service health for critical services. (7) Add remediation subflows for recurring alerts once stable. Measure compression and alert-to-incident ratios per source.</overview><pain>Thousands of alerts a day across tools; genuine issues missed Duplicate tickets for the same outage Alerts without CI or service context, so impact is guessed Incidents raised manually and late; MTTR is high No single operations view across monitoring tools</pain><phase>2</phase><requires>cmdb-csdm-foundation</requires><strong_terms>[{"re": "event management|AIOps", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "alert (noise|storm)|monitoring", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>Monitoring tools each raise their own alerts; the operations team drowns in noise, duplicates are handled by hand, and incidents are raised late or without service context. The pattern converges on OOB Event Management: connectors or push integrations from each monitoring tool, event rules to filter and transform, CI binding to the CMDB, alert correlation and grouping, alert-to-incident rules with service impact, and Operator Workspace — measured by noise reduction and time to detect.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:47</sys_created_on><sys_id>27017c1f692149c79a16726ca19e8c2b</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:47</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "event management|\\bevents?\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "alert|alarm|noise|storm", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "AIOps|observability|monitoring", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "SolarWinds|Splunk|Dynatrace|Datadog|Nagios|\\bSCOM\\b|Zabbix|\\bPRTG\\b|AppDynamics|New Relic|Prometheus|LogicMonitor", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "outage|major incident|\\bMTTR\\b|downtime", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "operator workspace|\\bNOC\\b|operations centre|operations center", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "correlat|dedup", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_4874dc995cad4b3cb3bda8c29e4e0be8
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[{"re": "field service|work order", "flags": "i"}]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>41</indicative_cases><key>csm-case-foundation</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>csm</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Customer Service Management case and contact-centre foundation</name><overview>Model the customer, then the work, then the channels. (1) Choose B2B (account/contact), B2C (consumer) or both, and integrate the CRM/billing system of record as the master (OOB Salesforce/Microsoft Dynamics spokes or IntegrationHub) — ServiceNow does not become the CRM. (2) Load products and install base only as far as routing and entitlements need them. (3) Define case types (extensions of the OOB case only where the process genuinely differs), categories, SLAs and entitlements. (4) Channels: inbound email actions, chat and phone (OpenFrame/CTI) creating interactions linked to cases; AWA queues, service channels, skills and capacity for push routing. (5) Customer portal with knowledge deflection and case communication. (6) Complaints on the OOB complaint management capability where regulated timeframes apply. (7) Middle/back-office requests via OOB request/task flows with SLAs. (8) CSM Configurable Workspace for agents and supervisors; dashboards for channel, FCR, AHT, SLA and CSAT.</overview><pain>Agents swivel between CRM, billing and ticketing to answer one question No single case history, so customers repeat themselves Complaints and escalations tracked in email and spreadsheets Back-office teams engaged by email with no SLA Channel volumes and handle time cannot be reported reliably</pain><phase>1</phase><requires/><strong_terms>[{"re": "\\bCSM\\b|customer service", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "contact cent(er|re)|call cent(er|re)", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>Customer or citizen enquiries arrive by phone, email and web into disconnected tools. Agents lack a single view of the customer, their products and prior cases; complaints and escalations are handled by email; middle- and back-office teams are engaged through side channels. The pattern converges on OOB CSM: an accounts/contacts (B2B) or consumers (B2C) data model, case types with SLAs, omni-channel intake with Advanced Work Assignment, a customer portal with knowledge, and requests to the middle/back office through OOB request and task flows — integrated with the CRM or billing system of record rather than replicating it.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:47</sys_created_on><sys_id>4874dc995cad4b3cb3bda8c29e4e0be8</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:47</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "\\bCSM\\b|customer service", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "contact.?cent(er|re)|call cent(er|re)|agent", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "customer (portal|case|complaint|experience)|citizen", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "omni.?channel|chat|email.to.case|telephony|\\bCTI\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "entitlement|contract|install base|product", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "complaint", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "customer|consumer|account", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "customers?", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "complain", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_4b16aa07c3c5429a93a6f33c5ef138c0
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[{"re": "privacy impact", "flags": "i"}]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>37</indicative_cases><key>irm-policy-compliance</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>irm</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>IRM / GRC policy, risk and compliance foundation</name><overview>Load the library once, scope entities well, then automate. (1) Agree frameworks in scope and import authority documents and citations (UCF where licensed) — never re-type regulations. (2) Model policies and policy statements and map them to citations; statements are what generate controls. (3) Design entity types with filters over existing platform data (business applications, business units, vendors) so entities and controls generate and stay current — owners come from those records. (4) Build a single risk framework (risk statements) and assessment methodology aligned to the client's matrix and appetite. (5) Operate: scheduled attestations, basic/script indicators on platform data (e.g. patching, access reviews), issues with due dates and escalations. (6) Add audit engagements and vendor risk only after the core is operating. (7) Report from the OOB workspaces. The IRM data model is used as-is; custom tables are not required.</overview><pain>Risk and control registers in spreadsheets with no single owner Audit evidence gathered manually for each request Controls not mapped to regulations, so coverage cannot be shown Issues from audits and control failures are not tracked to closure Duplicated assessments across teams (security, privacy, risk)</pain><phase>1</phase><requires/><strong_terms>[{"re": "\\bIRM\\b|\\bGRC\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "risk register|compliance|regulat", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>Risks, controls and compliance evidence live in spreadsheets and document libraries. Each audit or regulatory request (APRA CPS 230/234, ISO 27001, SOC 2, Essential Eight) triggers a scramble to find owners and evidence, control testing is inconsistent, and there is no line of sight from a policy to the controls that implement it and the issues raised against them. The pattern converges on the OOB IRM data model — authority documents and citations, policies and statements, entities, controls, risks, indicators and issues — loaded once, with attestation and automated control monitoring where platform data exists.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>4b16aa07c3c5429a93a6f33c5ef138c0</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "\\bIRM\\b|\\bGRC\\b|integrated risk", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "risk (register|management|assessment)", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "compliance|regulat|audit", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "policy|control|attest", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "ISO ?27001|SOC ?2|\\bAPRA\\b|CPS ?2(30|34)|Essential Eight|\\bIRAP\\b|\\bSOX\\b|\\bNIST\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "third.party|vendor risk", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "operational resilience|business continuity", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>
sys_update_xml.target_name: IRM / GRC policy, risk and compliance foundation

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_5c6ec6aa57e140f986af5947553a8c3e
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>6</indicative_cases><key>fsm-field-service</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>fsm</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Field Service Management</name><overview>Model the resources, then the work, then the experience. (1) Territories, skills, agent schedules and stockrooms (including van stock) loaded as reference data. (2) Work orders from CSM cases, ITSM incidents, assets and maintenance plans using OOB create actions. (3) Work order task templates by job type with required skills and parts. (4) Dispatcher Workspace with auto-assignment / Dynamic Scheduling where licensed; appointment booking windows. (5) Parts sourcing and consumption through OOB part requirements and transfer orders. (6) Now Mobile / FSM mobile app with offline, time, parts, signature and checklists. (7) Planned maintenance plans on assets. (8) Customer notifications and ETA. (9) KPIs: first-time fix, utilisation, travel, SLA.</overview><pain>Manual dispatch; poor utilisation and travel time Low first-time fix because parts and history are missing No customer appointment windows or ETA Preventive maintenance tracked outside the system Technicians complete paper job sheets</pain><phase>3</phase><requires>csm-case-foundation</requires><strong_terms>[{"re": "field service|work order|technician|dispatch", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>Field work is dispatched by phone and spreadsheet: technicians arrive without the right parts or history, first-visit resolution is low, and customers get no appointment certainty. The pattern converges on OOB Field Service Management: work orders and work order tasks from cases, incidents or planned maintenance; territories, skills and schedules; dispatcher workspace with (dynamic) scheduling; parts sourcing from stockrooms and van stock; the mobile agent app with offline capability; and customer appointment booking and notifications.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>5c6ec6aa57e140f986af5947553a8c3e</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "field service|\\bFSM\\b|work order", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "technician|engineer|crew|dispatch", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "on.?site|site visit|truck roll|first.?time fix", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "parts|spare|van stock|inventory", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "schedul|territor|route|appointment", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "maintenance|preventive|inspection|equipment", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "mobile app|offline", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_628bf2891d554853993138856ccb4ef2
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>6</indicative_cases><key>public-sector-case</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>psds,csm</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Public sector case, licensing and grants</name><overview>Settle compliance, then model services, then digitise. (1) Confirm hosting, classification (e.g. OFFICIAL / PROTECTED), IRAP posture, encryption and records retention before data lands. (2) Use the CSM consumer model for residents and account/contact for businesses. (3) Configure application/case types with the PSDS or Licensing & Permitting / Grants capabilities where licensed — stages, eligibility rules, assessment tasks, decisions, issued licences/grants with conditions and renewals. (4) Citizen portal with identity (e.g. state digital ID via SSO where available), status tracking and information requests. (5) Inspections on mobile. (6) Statutory timeframe SLAs and reporting. (7) Records retention via archive/destroy rules aligned to the retention schedule.</overview><pain>Citizens phone and email for status Officers re-key applications from PDF forms Inconsistent eligibility and assessment decisions Records retention and FOI evidence are manual Hosting and security classification unclear for cloud services</pain><phase>3</phase><requires>csm-case-foundation</requires><strong_terms>[{"re": "council|government|agency|citizen|resident", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "permit|licensing application|grant", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>An agency or council runs citizen-facing services — enquiries, complaints, licences, permits or grants — on legacy case systems, forms and spreadsheets. Citizens cannot see progress, officers re-key data, eligibility and assessment are inconsistent, and compliance (records, privacy, IRAP/PROTECTED) is hard to evidence. The pattern converges on ServiceNow Public Sector Digital Services capabilities where licensed (citizen portal, case, licensing and permitting, grants) on the CSM data model, with records governance and hosting/classification requirements settled first.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>628bf2891d554853993138856ccb4ef2</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "public sector|government|council|agency|department of|ministry|state|federal|citizen|resident|constituent", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "licen[cs]e(s|ing)? and permit|permit|licensing application|registration", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "grant(s)?\\b|funding application|assessment panel", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "case management|casework|complaint|311|enquir", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "PROTECTED|\\bIRAP\\b|data sovereignty|\\bFOI\\b|privacy act", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "eligibility|assessment|inspection", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_708c573d6514412a95254bedf01bfc4a
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>5</indicative_cases><key>esg-sustainability</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>esg</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>ESG and sustainability reporting</name><overview>Define once, collect with evidence, report with traceability. (1) Agree frameworks (e.g. AASB S2/ISSB, GRI) and build the metric library with units and calculation rules. (2) Model reporting entities (legal entities, sites, business units) reusing platform data. (3) Collection schedules generate tasks to named owners with evidence attachments and validation ranges. (4) Review/approval with rejection loop. (5) Calculations (e.g. emissions factors) configured, not coded, and versioned. (6) Targets, goals and initiatives tracked against baselines. (7) Supplier questionnaires via the supplier/vendor portal. (8) Disclosure reports with drill-down to evidence. Source systems (energy retailers, fleet, HR) integrate via import sets or IntegrationHub where volume justifies it.</overview><pain>ESG data gathered by email and spreadsheet each cycle No evidence trail for assurance Targets and initiatives not tracked between reports Supplier ESG data inconsistent Multiple frameworks require the same metric in different forms</pain><phase>3</phase><requires/><strong_terms>[{"re": "\\bESG\\b|carbon|emission|sustainab|AASB S2", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>ESG data (energy, emissions, workforce, supplier information) is collected by email and spreadsheet from many owners ahead of each reporting cycle. Evidence is hard to trace, targets are not tracked between cycles, and new mandatory climate disclosures (e.g. AASB S2 in Australia) raise the assurance bar. The pattern converges on OOB ESG Management where licensed: a metric and framework library, data collection tasks to owners with evidence, calculations, targets and goals, supplier ESG questionnaires, and audit-ready disclosure reporting.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>708c573d6514412a95254bedf01bfc4a</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "\\bESG\\b|sustainab|environmental, social", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "carbon|emission|scope [123]|net zero|greenhouse|\\bGHG\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "climate (disclosure|report)|AASB S2|\\bISSB\\b|\\bTCFD\\b|\\bCSRD\\b|\\bGRI\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "disclosure|metric|target|evidence|audit trail", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "energy|waste|water", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "supplier (ESG|questionnaire)", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_7663f4d384ef408a8ba3062e8c27a96c
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[{"re": "security incident", "flags": "i"}]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>168</indicative_cases><key>itsm-consolidation</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>itsm</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>ITSM consolidation and legacy service-desk migration</name><overview>Adopt, don't adapt. (1) Load the foundation first: users, groups, departments, locations and companies from the authoritative identity/HR source, plus a minimal CSDM service layer (business services and offerings) so incidents and requests carry a service. (2) Stand up Incident, Request, Problem, Change and Knowledge on OOB processes and states; configure, don't script. (3) Route with assignment rules / data lookups driven by service offering and category, backed by a rationalised group model (evidence itsm.routing). (4) Rationalise the catalogue to owned, used items and build fulfilment in Flow Designer, not legacy workflow. (5) Harmonise SLAs into one matrix with schedules and pause conditions. (6) Migrate open tickets only, with a source reference; archive closed history unless there is a regulatory need. (7) Put agents in Service Operations Workspace and managers on one dashboard. Anything customised in a legacy instance is re-assessed against OOB before it is rebuilt.</overview><pain>Agents swivel between tools; no single view of a user's tickets SLAs and priorities are calculated differently per tool, so performance reports are disputed Assignment groups and categories have grown organically — misrouting and reassignment loops Previous customisation makes upgrades slow and risky Knowledge is scattered and not linked to incidents, so first-contact resolution stays low</pain><phase>1</phase><requires/><strong_terms>[{"re": "\\bITSM\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "service desk", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "incident management", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>IT support runs across several tools (or an old, heavily customised ServiceNow instance). Tickets, SLAs and knowledge are fragmented, reporting is not trusted and every change to the tool is expensive. The pattern converges on out-of-the-box Incident, Request, Problem, Change and Knowledge on a clean data foundation (users, groups, locations, services), with a controlled historical-data decision rather than a full lift-and-shift.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>7663f4d384ef408a8ba3062e8c27a96c</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "\\bITSM\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "service desk", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "incident", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "\\brequest\\b|catalog", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "change (management|request)", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "legacy|remedy|cherwell|jira|ivanti|zendesk|multiple (tools|systems)", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "consolidat|migrat", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "\\bSLA\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "tickets?", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "help ?desk", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_7b4d65824e3147e0ab19ef6bd011d80c
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>8</indicative_cases><key>app-engine-greenfield</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>app_engine</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Greenfield scoped application (App Engine)</name><overview>Prove the gap, design small, secure first, test always. (1) Fit-to-standard: search OOB apps and existing tables (evidence ae.fit); only proceed with a design-authority decision. (2) Scoped application created with App Engine Studio or the Fluent SDK (now-sdk) — source-controlled. (3) Minimal data model: one primary table (extend Task only if work is assigned and SLA-tracked), child/reference tables only where needed; choices and properties over hard-coding. (4) Roles and ACLs from a persona matrix before any UI. (5) Flow Designer for approvals, notifications and integrations; no business-rule workflows. (6) UI Builder workspace for fulfillers, portal/Employee Center record producer for requesters. (7) ATF from the first sprint: critical path plus one access test per persona. (8) Governance: owner, App Engine Management Center or pipeline, app repository deployment, support model, and a custom-table count against entitlement. The workbench greenfield skeleton seeds the component list; this pattern adds the governance and evidence around it.</overview><pain>Critical process lives in a spreadsheet or legacy database with no audit trail No approvals, SLAs or notifications Previous quick builds became unowned technical debt Custom-table licence consumption unknown No standard for citizen developers</pain><phase>3</phase><requires/><strong_terms>[{"re": "App Engine|low.?code|custom app|scoped app", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "spreadsheet|access database|sharepoint list|paper form", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>A business process has no fit in an OOB application and runs on spreadsheets, an Access/Lotus database or a SharePoint list. The client wants it on the platform quickly without creating unmanaged technical debt. The pattern converges on a governed scoped application: fit-to-standard check first, a minimal data model extending Task only where work is assigned, roles and ACLs designed up front, Flow Designer for logic, a workspace/portal UI, ATF from day one, and App Engine governance (Management Center, pipelines, custom-table entitlement) — built with App Engine Studio or the Fluent SDK.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>7b4d65824e3147e0ab19ef6bd011d80c</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "App Engine|App Engine Studio|\\bAES\\b|low.?code|no.?code", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "custom (app|application)|scoped app|bespoke|build (an|a new) app", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "spreadsheet|access database|lotus notes|sharepoint list|paper form|manual (process|register)", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "citizen develop|fusion team", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "Fluent|now.?sdk|\\bIDE\\b", "flags": ""}, {"re": "register|tracker|approval process", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "\\bregister\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "\\btrack(ing|er)?\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "approv(al|e)", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "onboard", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "\\bform\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "new (app|application|system)", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_8d626f620b62477fb3d9517346e13cf8
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>18</indicative_cases><key>s2p-procurement</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>s2p,integrationhub</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Source-to-pay and procurement operations</name><overview>ServiceNow engages, the ERP records. (1) Guided buying intake in Employee Center routing to catalogue, preferred supplier or sourcing. (2) Purchase request approvals by budget/amount, then requisition/PO creation in the ERP via spoke or API; ERP numbers written back. (3) Supplier Lifecycle Operations for onboarding: supplier portal questionnaire, risk/compliance checks (link to IRM vendor risk where licensed), ERP supplier creation on approval. (4) Accounts Payable Operations for invoice exceptions and supplier queries as cases with SLAs. (5) Master data synchronised by ERP ID only; no parallel financial records. (6) Dashboards for cycle time, onboarding time and exception ageing.</overview><pain>Requesters email procurement; no guided buying Supplier onboarding takes weeks with manual risk checks Invoice exceptions handled by email between AP, buyers and approvers No visibility of procurement workload or cycle time Point tools duplicate ERP data</pain><phase>3</phase><requires>integration-hub</requires><strong_terms>[{"re": "procure|supplier|accounts payable|invoice", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>Procurement and accounts payable teams juggle suppliers, contracts, portals, email and spreadsheets around the ERP. Requesters do not know how to buy, supplier onboarding is slow and risky, and invoice exceptions bounce between teams. The pattern converges on the ServiceNow procurement and finance operations layer — Procurement Service Management / Sourcing and Procurement Operations, Supplier Lifecycle Operations and Accounts Payable Operations where licensed — as the engagement layer over the ERP, which stays the system of record for POs, invoices and payments.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>8d626f620b62477fb3d9517346e13cf8</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "source.to.pay|\\bS2P\\b|procure.to.pay|\\bP2P\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "procurement|purchasing|purchase (order|request|requisition)|sourcing", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "supplier|vendor (onboarding|management|lifecycle)", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "accounts payable|invoice|\\bAP\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "SAP Ariba|Coupa|Oracle|\\bSAP\\b|\\bERP\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "spend|contract", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_8d97fa25f5114eb4b6ee61ef9fdc7882
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>51</indicative_cases><key>managed-service-ops</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products/><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Platform managed service and continual improvement</name><overview>Run the platform as a product. (1) Operating model: platform owner, product owners per workflow, platform team and managed-service partner with a RACI and monthly governance forum. (2) One backlog: an enhancement/defect intake (record producer to SPM demand, Agile stories or rm_enhancement) with value/effort scoring. (3) Release cadence (e.g. fortnightly minor, quarterly major) with quality gates: peer review, Instance Scan, ATF suite, change approval, and batched update sets. (4) Proactive health monitoring: a scheduled read-only health check with thresholds raising incidents to the platform team; integration and job failure alerts; use Instance Observer / performance dashboards where available. (5) Environment management: clone calendar, exclusion/preserver lists and post-clone cleanup. (6) Managed-service SLAs and a monthly report pack. (7) Continual improvement register fed by adoption and value metrics. Everything uses OOB records; the only custom element is the scheduled health check script, justified because it aggregates signals no single OOB job reports.</overview><pain>Enhancement requests arrive by email with no prioritisation or visibility Platform issues found by users, not by monitoring Releases are irregular and risky; no release calendar Specialist knowledge sits with one person or a departed partner Leaders cannot see platform value or adoption trends</pain><phase>2</phase><requires>platform-upgrade-debt</requires><strong_terms>[{"re": "managed service|after go.live|\\bBAU\\b|platform health", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>After go-live the client lacks specialist capacity to run, upgrade and improve ServiceNow. Enhancement requests pile up in email, platform health (performance, errors, stuck jobs, integrations) is checked only when users complain, and releases are ad hoc. The pattern converges on a platform operating model: a governed demand/enhancement backlog, release cadence with update-set and ATF gates, proactive platform health monitoring with thresholds, a managed-service SLA and reporting pack, and a continual-improvement register tied to adoption and value.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>8d97fa25f5114eb4b6ee61ef9fdc7882</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "managed service|as.a.service|\\bAMS\\b|run (and|&) (optimi|improve)|\\bBAU\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "ongoing support|post.go.live|hypercare|after go.live", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "platform (owner|team|operations|health)|instance health", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "backlog|enhancement|continual (service )?improvement|\\bCSI\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "performance|slow|queue|scheduled job|errors?", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "capacity|specialist|skills? gap|contractor", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "governance|release cadence|clone", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_93dbb3f9c9374c8b88cbf9fbbc6dee11
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>17</indicative_cases><key>platform-upgrade-debt</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products/><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Platform upgrade, customisation and technical-debt remediation</name><overview>Measure, triage, protect, then upgrade on a cadence. (1) Run evidence on a fresh production clone: release history, skipped records, customisation footprint, Instance Scan and ATF coverage. (2) Triage every skipped record and customised OOB file with a four-way disposition — revert to base, merge (retain with the new baseline changes), retain as justified customisation, or retire — owned by the relevant process owner. (3) Build the safety net before touching code: ATF suites for the critical journeys, scheduled Instance Scan with agreed suites. (4) Remediate in waves by application, reverting first because it removes future upgrade cost. (5) Replace deprecated features and legacy workflows with Flow Designer and current plugins per the release notes. (6) Upgrade using the documented clone → upgrade → ATF → UAT → promote runbook, with Upgrade Center / Upgrade Plan where available. (7) Hold the line with development standards, peer review and scan gates on update sets. Report the debt trend monthly.</overview><pain>Upgrades take months and are deferred; the instance falls out of support Thousands of skipped records with no owner or decision Customised OOB scripts break silently after each upgrade No regression automation; testing is manual and incomplete Deprecated plugins and legacy workflows block new capabilities</pain><phase>2</phase><requires/><strong_terms>[{"re": "upgrade|technical debt|skipped", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>The instance is one or more family releases behind because every upgrade is painful: thousands of skipped records, heavy customisation of OOB scripts and forms, legacy workflows, and no automated regression. The pattern converges on a repeatable upgrade capability: evidence-based debt inventory (skipped records, customer updates, Instance Scan findings, deprecated features), a triage decision per item (revert to OOB, retain and merge, rebuild, or retire), an ATF regression suite for critical journeys, and a clone-upgrade-test cadence that keeps the instance within N-1.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>93dbb3f9c9374c8b88cbf9fbbc6dee11</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "upgrade|family release|release (behind|n-?[12])|patch", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "technical debt|tech debt", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "customi[sz]ation|custom (code|script)|skipped (record|update)", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "back to (OOB|out.of.the.box|baseline)|return to OOB|reimplement", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "instance scan|health ?scan|impact", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "deprecat|end of life|\\bEOL\\b|legacy workflow", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "regression|\\bATF\\b|clone", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "behind|out of support|release", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_9502ffca8cf0439989ddf6b7b57dddea
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>14</indicative_cases><key>secops-sir</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>secops_sir</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Security Incident Response and SecOps foundation</name><overview>Ingest, prioritise, respond, learn — with access designed first. (1) Security roles and group model: SOC analysts, handlers, managers; IT responders get tasks, not incidents; platform admins do not get SIR access by default. (2) Ingest from the SIEM/EDR via the OOB store integrations (or the SIR ingestion APIs / email parsing as fallback); correlate duplicates. (3) Severity calculator using CI business criticality, data classification and category — this depends on the CMDB/CSDM pattern. (4) Playbooks (Playbook/PAD) for the top categories from evidence (e.g. phishing, malware, account compromise, data loss). (5) Response tasks and SIR requests to IT groups with SLAs; change requests for remediation via the OOB link. (6) Threat intelligence enrichment using licensed or free feeds via OOB integrations. (7) Major security incident, post-incident review, and a notifiable data breach assessment captured on the incident. (8) SOC dashboard. No custom tables; extend categories and playbooks, not the data model.</overview><pain>Alerts triaged manually from the SIEM; no audit trail Severity decided by judgement, not business impact Containment depends on individual analysts; no playbooks IT teams engaged by chat with no SLA or evidence Post-incident reviews and notifiable data breach assessments not consistently recorded</pain><phase>2</phase><requires>cmdb-csdm-foundation</requires><strong_terms>[{"re": "security incident|\\bSOC\\b|\\bSIEM\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "phishing|malware", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>Security alerts from the SIEM and EDR tools are triaged in email, chat and spreadsheets. There is no consistent severity model, containment steps depend on who is on shift, IT teams are engaged informally, and post-incident reviews and regulator notifications are hard to evidence. The pattern converges on OOB Security Incident Response: ingestion from security tools into security incidents, a calculated severity using CMDB business context, playbooks for the top incident categories, response tasks to IT groups, threat-intelligence enrichment, restricted access, and post-incident review and notification tracking.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>9502ffca8cf0439989ddf6b7b57dddea</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "security incident|\\bSIR\\b|SecOps|security operations", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "\\bSOC\\b|\\bSIEM\\b|Splunk|Sentinel|QRadar|CrowdStrike|Defender|\\bXDR\\b|\\bEDR\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "phishing|malware|ransomware|breach|threat", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "playbook|runbook|containment", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "threat intel|observable|IOC\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "notifiable|\\bOAIC\\b|\\bNDB\\b|post.incident", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>0</indicative_cases><key>vr-tenable-cmdb</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>secops_vr,itom_visibility</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Tenable vulnerability ingestion without a CMDB foundation</name><overview>Foundation first, then matching. (1) Agree the in-scope asset classes and an authoritative population source (Discovery or a Service Graph Connector such as SCCM/Intune/Jamf) — Tenable is a consumer of the CMDB, not its source. (2) Make the IRE deterministic for those classes: serial number first, then name/FQDN; IP is a last-resort lookup, never an identifier. (3) Give Tenable the right reconciliation precedence so it can enrich but never overwrite authoritative attributes. (4) Order the VR CI lookup rules to match on the attributes both sides actually carry (from the evidence), and review the host import map. (5) Decide the unmatched policy — create unclassed hardware for triage, or hold in discovered items — and schedule the reapply job. (6) Populate support group and business criticality so assignment and risk scoring work without custom code. (7) Make the state visible: CMDB Health for the in-scope classes and VR match-rate reporting. All of this is configuration captured in an update set; no custom integration is required.</overview><pain>Vulnerable items (VITs) not matched to CIs, so no assignment group, no business criticality, no remediation owner Tenable becomes the de facto CMDB source — unclassed hardware sprawl and duplicates Reports count findings, not assets; SLA and exposure figures are not defensible Prior attempts to bypass CI matching with custom integrations create technical debt and upgrade risk</pain><phase>0</phase><requires/><strong_terms>[{"re": "tenable", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "vulnerab", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "discovered item", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>Vulnerability Response is ingesting Tenable findings, but the CMDB has no reliable population, identification, reconciliation or ownership rules. Vulnerable items land on unmatched discovered items or unclassed hardware, nothing routes to an owner, and risk scoring has no CI context. The fix is a CMDB foundation for the in-scope asset classes plus correctly ordered CI lookup and reconciliation rules — not a custom integration that bypasses matching.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>9ad6efafe3d645c1bce9ff6b75af7152</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "tenable", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "vulnerab", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "\\bVR\\b", "flags": ""}, {"re": "cmdb", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "ci\\s*lookup", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "unmatched", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "discovered item", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_a828e5429bda4f57b75d7e4a3331f23f
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>7</indicative_cases><key>dpo-privacy</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>privacy</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Privacy management and data governance</name><overview>Register, assess, respond, protect. (1) Privacy register of processing activities linked to business applications (CSDM) and data categories. (2) Threshold assessment → full PIA workflow with privacy officer approval (Privacy Management / IRM assessments). (3) Data subject request intake (portal/email), identity verification, fulfilment tasks across system owners, statutory timers. (4) Breach assessment linked to security incidents (SIR) with the notifiable-data-breach decision and dates. (5) Platform protection: data classification on sensitive fields, field encryption (Cloud Encryption / Column Level Encryption where licensed), role-based field access, clone data anonymisation/cleanup, and archive/destroy rules. (6) Privacy dashboard.</overview><pain>PIAs done in documents with no register Access and deletion requests tracked in inboxes, deadlines missed Breach assessment inconsistent and slow Personal information in ServiceNow not classified or masked Production data copied to sub-production clones unmasked</pain><phase>3</phase><requires/><strong_terms>[{"re": "privacy|personal information|\\bDSAR\\b|\\bPIA\\b", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>Privacy obligations (Australian Privacy Act and APPs, GDPR for offshore customers) are managed through documents and email: privacy impact assessments are inconsistent, data subject requests are tracked in inboxes, breaches are assessed ad hoc, and nobody can show where personal information lives in ServiceNow itself. The pattern converges on OOB Privacy Management where licensed (processing activities, PIAs, data subject requests, breach assessment) plus platform data governance: data classification, encryption and masking, data privacy/anonymisation for clones and exports, and retention rules.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>a828e5429bda4f57b75d7e4a3331f23f</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "privacy|personal information|\\bPII\\b|\\bGDPR\\b|Privacy Act|\\bOAIC\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "\\bAPPs?\\b", "flags": ""}, {"re": "data subject|access request|\\bDSAR\\b|right to (access|erasure)", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "\\bPIA\\b|privacy impact|\\bDPIA\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "data breach|notifiable", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "data governance|data classification|data residency|retention", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "masking|encryption|anonymi[sz]", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "personal data|customer data protection", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_e96633990a4b4bd0a7aa9de3d4f7fa00
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>18</indicative_cases><key>telecom-tsm</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>telecom,csm</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Telecommunications service and order management</name><overview>Inventory, assurance, then orders. (1) CSM foundation for accounts, contacts, sites and sold products. (2) Service inventory (customer-facing services) related to network inventory — populated from OSS/inventory systems via Service Graph / IntegrationHub, not manual entry. (3) Network events into Event Management; network incidents with impacted services and accounts calculated from inventory relationships. (4) Proactive notification and case linkage for impacted accounts. (5) Product catalogue and Order Management: product offerings, specifications, order decomposition and orchestration to OSS/BSS. (6) eBonding with partners using OOB/IntegrationHub patterns. (7) Assurance and order dashboards. Table names for the telecom apps vary by release — confirm with evidence tel.apps before configuration.</overview><pain>Agents cannot see which customer services are affected by a network fault Orders stall across OSS/BSS hand-offs B2B customers learn of outages before the provider tells them Duplicate product definitions in several systems Manual ticket exchange with wholesale partners</pain><phase>3</phase><requires>csm-case-foundation,itom-aiops-event</requires><strong_terms>[{"re": "telco|telecom|network outage|\\bOSS\\b|\\bBSS\\b", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>A telecommunications provider runs customer service, order fulfilment and network assurance in separate OSS/BSS tools. Agents cannot see network impact on a customer's services, orders stall between systems, and B2B customers receive late outage information. The pattern converges on ServiceNow Telecommunications Service Management and Order Management (where licensed) on the CSM foundation: a product and service catalogue, customer-facing service inventory linked to network inventory, order decomposition and orchestration to OSS, and proactive service impact from network events to customer cases.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>e96633990a4b4bd0a7aa9de3d4f7fa00</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "telco|telecom|carrier|network operator|\\bISP\\b|mobile operator|\\bNBN\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "\\bTSM\\b|telecommunications service", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "order management|\\bOMT\\b|product catalog(ue)?|service order|fulfil(l)?ment", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "network inventory|\\bTNI\\b|service inventory|\\bOSS\\b|\\bBSS\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "outage|network event|service impact|fault", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "enterprise customer|B2B customer|bond|eBonding", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_f0c40ed7d7ac4c1a957aafe864f1f114
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[{"re": "medical device|biomed", "flags": "i"}]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>29</indicative_cases><key>itam-ham-sam</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>itam_ham,itam_sam</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Hardware and software asset management (HAM / SAM)</name><overview>Clean the foundation, then run the lifecycle, then prove the licence position. (1) Normalise hardware and software content (Content Service) so models and publishers are consistent. (2) Configure model categories so CIs and assets create each other one-to-one, and apply OOB asset–CI field and status synchronisation — no custom sync scripts. (3) Run the hardware lifecycle on OOB states and substates, stockrooms, transfer orders and HAM workspace refresh/disposal. (4) For SAM, pick priority publishers (by spend and audit risk), load entitlements from contracts/POs with correct licence metrics, and let OOB publisher packs reconcile installs to entitlements. (5) Turn on reclamation rules for high-cost, low-use titles. (6) Reconcile with finance on asset tag/cost centre. (7) Report from the HAM and SAM workspaces. Custom asset tables are not required.</overview><pain>Asset register does not match the CMDB or the finance fixed-asset register Hardware lifecycle and stock are tracked in spreadsheets; refresh and disposal are late No defensible licence position for major publishers; audit exposure Software spend on unused installs and subscriptions (no reclamation) Models and manufacturers are not normalised, so reports split one product many ways</pain><phase>2</phase><requires>cmdb-csdm-foundation</requires><strong_terms>[{"re": "\\bHAM\\b|\\bSAM\\b|\\bITAM\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "licen[cs]e (position|compliance)|software asset|hardware asset", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>Asset records are incomplete or disconnected from the CMDB, hardware lifecycle (request, receive, deploy, refresh, dispose) is run from spreadsheets, and software spend is justified without a defensible licence position. Vendor audits and refresh programmes become fire drills. The pattern converges on OOB Hardware Asset Management and Software Asset Management: normalised models, one-to-one asset–CI synchronisation, lifecycle states and stockrooms, entitlements loaded from contracts, and reconciliation of installs to entitlements for the priority publishers.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>f0c40ed7d7ac4c1a957aafe864f1f114</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "\\bHAM\\b|hardware asset", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "\\bSAM\\b|software asset|licen[cs]e (position|compliance|optimi|audit)", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "\\bITAM\\b|asset (management|lifecycle|register)", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "stockroom|procure|refresh|disposal|retire", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "entitlement|true.?up|vendor audit|microsoft|oracle|adobe", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "asset", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "normali[sz]", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "laptops?|devices?|hardware", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "licen[cs]es?", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_f57c6db779734f4ea34b1ec5d8dedf38
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>20</indicative_cases><key>esm-workplace</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>esm</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Enterprise service management: workplace, facilities, legal, finance</name><overview>One front door, OOB department apps first, a template for the rest. (1) Employee Center with a single taxonomy covering IT, HR and the business departments. (2) Use the OOB department application where the client is licensed — Workplace Service Delivery (spaces, reservations, facilities cases), Legal Service Delivery (requests, matters, legal counsel centre), Finance/Accounts Payable operations. (3) For other departments, a standard onboarding template: department group(s), catalogue category, record producers onto an existing request/case table (or a single shared ESM scoped table approved once), SLAs, knowledge base, notifications and dashboard — no per-department custom tables. (4) Confidential departments (legal) get contextual security from the start. (5) Report per department and across the enterprise. Note custom-table licensing: each new table counts against App Engine entitlements.</overview><pain>Each department runs its own inbox and spreadsheet Employees do not know where to go for non-IT help No workload, SLA or satisfaction data outside IT Departments buy point tools that duplicate the platform Facilities space and desk usage unknown after hybrid-work changes</pain><phase>3</phase><requires>hrsd-foundation</requires><strong_terms>[{"re": "facilit|workplace|desk booking", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "legal (request|service)", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>Business departments beyond IT — facilities, legal, finance, marketing — run their services from shared mailboxes and spreadsheets. Employees do not know where to ask, departments cannot show workload or SLA, and each team asks for its own tool. The pattern converges on one enterprise service model on the platform: OOB department applications where licensed (Workplace Service Delivery, Legal Service Delivery, Finance Operations), and a governed, templated case/request pattern for other departments, all behind Employee Center with a shared taxonomy.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>f57c6db779734f4ea34b1ec5d8dedf38</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "\\bESM\\b|enterprise service management", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "workplace|facilit|space|desk booking|reservation|hybrid work|move", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "legal (request|matter|service|intake)|contract review|\\bNDA\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "finance (operations|request)|accounts payable|procurement request", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "shared services|back.office|department(s)?\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "email inbox|shared mailbox|spreadsheet", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "buildings?|office", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

sys_update_xml.name: x_1577958_dsb_pattern_feb9570f3df64d249bd135c8a0a1bfa2
sys_update_xml.payload: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><active>true</active><exclude_terms>[]</exclude_terms><indicative_cases>27</indicative_cases><key>emergency-response</key><library_version>1.5</library_version><licence_products>emergency</licence_products><min_hits>2</min_hits><name>Emergency outreach and workforce wellbeing (Safe Workplace)</name><overview>Contactable people, pre-built outreach, automatic follow-up. (1) Keep user mobile numbers, locations (with coordinates) and managers current via the HR/identity sync. (2) Configure the OOB outreach capability (Emergency Outreach / Safe Workplace where licensed) with channels: email, SMS (Notify/Twilio), Now Mobile and Microsoft Teams. (3) Outreach templates per scenario (bushfire, flood, building evacuation, cyber) with response options. (4) Follow-up flow: "need help" creates a welfare task; non-responders get reminders then escalate to managers. (5) Crisis dashboard with live counts; restricted role for the crisis team. (6) Run a test outreach each quarter. Response data is sensitive — access limited and retention defined.</overview><pain>No reliable way to reach staff in an affected area Responses tracked in spreadsheets People needing help are not followed up promptly Contact details and locations are out of date No audit trail for the crisis response</pain><phase>3</phase><requires/><strong_terms>[{"re": "emergency|bushfire|flood|crisis|are you safe|outreach", "flags": "i"}]</strong_terms><summary>When an emergency happens — bushfire, flood, cyber event, pandemic — the organisation cannot quickly reach affected staff, confirm they are safe, and coordinate help. Contact lists are out of date, responses come back by email and text, and follow-up is manual. The pattern converges on OOB Emergency Outreach / Safe Workplace capabilities where licensed (or a governed outreach flow): targeted outreach by location or group through email, SMS, mobile and Teams, response tracking, automatic follow-up tasks for people who need help, and dashboards for the crisis team.</summary><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>feb9570f3df64d249bd135c8a0a1bfa2</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><triggers>[{"re": "emergency|crisis|disaster|bushfire|flood|storm|cyclone|pandemic|\\bCOVID\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "outreach|check.?in|welfare check|are you safe|mass notification", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "wellbeing|health and safety|\\bWHS\\b|\\bOHS\\b", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "business continuity|\\bBCP\\b|crisis management", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "workforce|employees? (safety|location)|travel", "flags": "i"}, {"re": "\\bSMS\\b|Notify|Teams", "flags": "i"}]</triggers><verification_notes/><verified>false</verified><verified_on/><verified_release/></x_1577958_dsb_pattern></record_update>

function _tbl(t){ return gs.tableExists(t); }
function _fieldOk(t, path){ var gr = new GlideRecord(t); var parts = path.split('.'); for (var i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) { if (!gr.isValidField(parts[i])) return false; if (i < parts.length - 1) { var ref = gr.getElement(parts[i]).getReferenceTable(); if (!ref) return false; gr = new GlideRecord(ref); } } return true; }
function _badField(t, q){ if (!q) return ''; var conds = String(q).split(/\^NQ|\^OR|\^/); for (var i = 0; i < conds.length; i++) { var m = conds[i].match(/^([a-z0-9_.]+)/); if (!m) continue; var f = m[1].replace(/\.$/, ''); if (f === 'sys_id') continue; if (!_fieldOk(t, f)) return f; } return ''; }
function count(t, q){ if (!_tbl(t)) return 'table not found'; var bad = _badField(t, q); if (bad) { DSB_NOTES.push(t + ': field not found ' + bad); return 'field not found: ' + bad; } var ga = new GlideAggregate(t); if (q) ga.addEncodedQuery(q); ga.addAggregate('COUNT'); ga.query(); return ga.next() ? parseInt(ga.getAggregate('COUNT'), 10) : 0; }
function groupCount(t, f, q, lim){ if (!_tbl(t)) return 'table not found'; var bad = _badField(t, q) || (_fieldOk(t, f) ? '' : f); if (bad) { DSB_NOTES.push(t + ': field not found ' + bad); return 'field not found: ' + bad; } var rows = []; var ga = new GlideAggregate(t); if (q) ga.addEncodedQuery(q); ga.addAggregate('COUNT'); ga.groupBy(f); ga.query(); var guard = 0; while (ga.next() && guard++ < 5000) rows.push([ga.getDisplayValue(f) || '(empty)', parseInt(ga.getAggregate('COUNT'), 10)]); rows.sort(function(a, b){ return b[1] - a[1]; }); var o = {}; rows.slice(0, lim || 50).forEach(function(r){ o[r[0]] = r[1]; }); if (rows.length > (lim || 50)) o['(other groups)'] = rows.length - (lim || 50); return o; }
function groupSet(t, f, q){ var o = {}; if (!_tbl(t) || !_fieldOk(t, f) || _badField(t, q)) return o; var ga = new GlideAggregate(t); if (q) ga.addEncodedQuery(q); ga.addAggregate('COUNT'); ga.groupBy(f); ga.query(); while (ga.next()) o[ga.getValue(f)] = parseInt(ga.getAggregate('COUNT'), 10); return o; }
function isNum(x){ return typeof x === 'number' && !isNaN(x); }
function diff(a, b){ return (isNum(a) && isNum(b)) ? a - b : 'n/a'; }
function pct(t, q, base){ var b = count(t, base); if (!isNum(b) || !b) return isNum(b) ? 0 : b; var c = count(t, base ? base + '^' + q : q); return isNum(c) ? Math.round(100 * c / b) : c; }
function hasField(t, f){ return _tbl(t) && _fieldOk(t, f); }
function dsbPrint(key, out){ if (DSB_NOTES.length) out.dsb_notes = DSB_NOTES; var LIM = 60000; var s = JSON.stringify(out, null, 1); if (s.length > LIM) s = JSON.stringify(out); var cut = [], loops = 0; while (s.length > LIM && loops++ < 60) { var bigK = null, bigL = 0; for (var k in out) { if (k === 'key' || k === 'dsb_truncated' || !out[k] || typeof out[k] !== 'object') continue; var l = JSON.stringify(out[k]).length; if (l > bigL) { bigL = l; bigK = k; } } if (!bigK) break; var v = out[bigK]; if (Object.prototype.toString.call(v) === '[object Array]' && v.length > 10) { out[bigK] = v.slice(0, Math.floor(v.length / 2)); cut.push(bigK + ' kept ' + out[bigK].length + ' of ' + v.length); } else { out[bigK] = 'omitted: ' + bigL + ' characters'; cut.push(bigK + ' omitted'); } out.dsb_truncated = cut; s = JSON.stringify(out); } gs.print('=== DSB-EVIDENCE ' + key + ' ===\n' + s); }
var MAX_ROWS = 5000;
var LAST90 = 'sys_created_onRELATIVEGT@dayofweek@ago@90';
var d = new GlideAggregate('alm_hardware'); d.addNotNullQuery('ci'); d.addAggregate('COUNT'); d.groupBy('ci'); d.addHaving('COUNT', '>', 1); d.query(); var multi = 0; while (d.next()) multi++;
gs.print('=== DSB-PVT itam ===\n' + JSON.stringify({
  hw_assets_active: count('alm_hardware', 'install_status!=7'),
  hw_assets_without_ci: count('alm_hardware', 'install_status!=7^ciISEMPTY'),
  cis_with_multiple_assets: multi,
  retired_asset_active_ci: count('alm_hardware', 'install_status=7^ci.install_status!=7'),
  in_use_no_assigned_to: count('alm_hardware', 'install_status=1^assigned_toISEMPTY'),
  entitlements: count('alm_license'),
  reconciliation_results: count('samp_sw_reconciliation_result'),
  ran: new GlideDateTime().getDisplayValue()}, null, 2));</body><data>{"kind": "script", "purpose": "PVT evidence for asset–CI integrity and lifecycle data quality. Compare with itam.hardware / itam.assetci.", "prereqs": null, "rollback": null}</data><kind>implementation</kind><modifies_data>false</modifies_data><pattern display_value="Hardware and software asset management (HAM / SAM)">f0c40ed7d7ac4c1a957aafe864f1f114</pattern><seq>2</seq><share_key/><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:54</sys_created_on><sys_id>2b7231a394a44565af17b1061ec24dd9</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:54</sys_updated_on><title>Post-implementation verification — ITAM (READ ONLY)</title></x_1577958_dsb_pattern_item></record_update>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern_item"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern_item action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><body>// DSB EVIDENCE esg.apps — READ ONLY.
// --- DSB helper prelude (read only; no personal information is printed) ---
var DSB_NOTES = [];
function _tbl(t){ return gs.tableExists(t); }
function _fieldOk(t, path){ var gr = new GlideRecord(t); var parts = path.split('.'); for (var i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) { if (!gr.isValidField(parts[i])) return false; if (i < parts.length - 1) { var ref = gr.getElement(parts[i]).getReferenceTable(); if (!ref) return false; gr = new GlideRecord(ref); } } return true; }
function _badField(t, q){ if (!q) return ''; var conds = String(q).split(/\^NQ|\^OR|\^/); for (var i = 0; i < conds.length; i++) { var m = conds[i].match(/^([a-z0-9_.]+)/); if (!m) continue; var f = m[1].replace(/\.$/, ''); if (f === 'sys_id') continue; if (!_fieldOk(t, f)) return f; } return ''; }
function count(t, q){ if (!_tbl(t)) return 'table not found'; var bad = _badField(t, q); if (bad) { DSB_NOTES.push(t + ': field not found ' + bad); return 'field not found: ' + bad; } var ga = new GlideAggregate(t); if (q) ga.addEncodedQuery(q); ga.addAggregate('COUNT'); ga.query(); return ga.next() ? parseInt(ga.getAggregate('COUNT'), 10) : 0; }
function groupCount(t, f, q, lim){ if (!_tbl(t)) return 'table not found'; var bad = _badField(t, q) || (_fieldOk(t, f) ? '' : f); if (bad) { DSB_NOTES.push(t + ': field not found ' + bad); return 'field not found: ' + bad; } var rows = []; var ga = new GlideAggregate(t); if (q) ga.addEncodedQuery(q); ga.addAggregate('COUNT'); ga.groupBy(f); ga.query(); var guard = 0; while (ga.next() && guard++ < 5000) rows.push([ga.getDisplayValue(f) || '(empty)', parseInt(ga.getAggregate('COUNT'), 10)]); rows.sort(function(a, b){ return b[1] - a[1]; }); var o = {}; rows.slice(0, lim || 50).forEach(function(r){ o[r[0]] = r[1]; }); if (rows.length > (lim || 50)) o['(other groups)'] = rows.length - (lim || 50); return o; }
function groupSet(t, f, q){ var o = {}; if (!_tbl(t) || !_fieldOk(t, f) || _badField(t, q)) return o; var ga = new GlideAggregate(t); if (q) ga.addEncodedQuery(q); ga.addAggregate('COUNT'); ga.groupBy(f); ga.query(); while (ga.next()) o[ga.getValue(f)] = parseInt(ga.getAggregate('COUNT'), 10); return o; }
function isNum(x){ return typeof x === 'number' && !isNaN(x); }
function diff(a, b){ return (isNum(a) && isNum(b)) ? a - b : 'n/a'; }
function pct(t, q, base){ var b = count(t, base); if (!isNum(b) || !b) return isNum(b) ? 0 : b; var c = count(t, base ? base + '^' + q : q); return isNum(c) ? Math.round(100 * c / b) : c; }
function hasField(t, f){ return _tbl(t) && _fieldOk(t, f); }
function dsbPrint(key, out){ if (DSB_NOTES.length) out.dsb_notes = DSB_NOTES; var LIM = 60000; var s = JSON.stringify(out, null, 1); if (s.length > LIM) s = JSON.stringify(out); var cut = [], loops = 0; while (s.length > LIM && loops++ < 60) { var bigK = null, bigL = 0; for (var k in out) { if (k === 'key' || k === 'dsb_truncated' || !out[k] || typeof out[k] !== 'object') continue; var l = JSON.stringify(out[k]).length; if (l > bigL) { bigL = l; bigK = k; } } if (!bigK) break; var v = out[bigK]; if (Object.prototype.toString.call(v) === '[object Array]' && v.length > 10) { out[bigK] = v.slice(0, Math.floor(v.length / 2)); cut.push(bigK + ' kept ' + out[bigK].length + ' of ' + v.length); } else { out[bigK] = 'omitted: ' + bigL + ' characters'; cut.push(bigK + ' omitted'); } out.dsb_truncated = cut; s = JSON.stringify(out); } gs.print('=== DSB-EVIDENCE ' + key + ' ===\n' + s); }
var MAX_ROWS = 5000;
var LAST90 = 'sys_created_onRELATIVEGT@dayofweek@ago@90';
function appInventory(scopes, names, tablePrefixes){
  var o = {release: gs.getProperty('glide.buildname', '(not set)'), store_apps: [], tables: {}};
  var q = []; scopes.forEach(function(s){ q.push('scopeSTARTSWITH' + s); }); names.forEach(function(n){ q.push('nameLIKE' + n); });
  if (q.length) { var sa = new GlideRecord('sys_store_app'); sa.addEncodedQuery(q.join('^OR')); sa.query(); while (sa.next()) o.store_apps.push(sa.getValue('name') + ' ' + sa.getValue('version') + (sa.getValue('active') == '1' || sa.getValue('active') == 'true' ? '' : ' (inactive)')); }
  var tq = []; tablePrefixes.forEach(function(p){ tq.push('nameSTARTSWITH' + p); });
  if (tq.length) { var t = new GlideRecord('sys_db_object'); t.addEncodedQuery(tq.join('^OR')); t.orderBy('name'); t.setLimit(150); t.query();
    while (t.next()) { var n = t.getValue('name'); var c = count(n); if (c !== 0) o.tables[n] = c; } }
  return o;
}
var out = appInventory(['sn_esg','sn_sust','sn_gf'], ['ESG','Sustainability','Carbon','Goal Framework'], ['sn_esg_','sn_gf_']);
out.key = 'esg.apps';
dsbPrint('esg.apps', out);</body><data>{"key": "esg.apps", "why": "Confirms ESG app presence and version", "unblocks": "Licensing check"}</data><kind>evidence_script</kind><modifies_data>false</modifies_data><pattern display_value="ESG and sustainability reporting">708c573d6514412a95254bedf01bfc4a</pattern><seq>0</seq><share_key/><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:56</sys_created_on><sys_id>421cd4f9c8b54ce8a38c99e538f20eb5</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:56</sys_updated_on><title>ESG Management applications and tables with data</title></x_1577958_dsb_pattern_item></record_update>

sys_update_xml.payload:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern_item"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern_item action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><body>// DSB IMPLEMENTATION em-test-events — DATA CHANGING (sub-prod). DRY RUN unless DRY_RUN = false.
var DRY_RUN = true;
var NODE = 'example-host01';   // <confirm> an existing CI name
var events = [
  {severity: '1', type: 'CPU', resource: 'cpu0', message_key: 'DSB_TEST_CPU_' + NODE, description: 'DSB test critical CPU'},
  {severity: '5', type: 'Info', resource: 'agent', message_key: 'DSB_TEST_INFO_' + NODE, description: 'DSB test informational'}
];
events.forEach(function(e){
  gs.print((DRY_RUN ? '[DRY RUN] ' : '') + JSON.stringify(e));
  if (DRY_RUN) return;
  var ev = new GlideRecord('em_event'); ev.initialize();
  ev.setValue('source', 'DSB_TEST'); ev.setValue('node', NODE); ev.setValue('type', e.type); ev.setValue('resource', e.resource);
  ev.setValue('severity', e.severity); ev.setValue('message_key', e.message_key); ev.setValue('description', e.description);
  gs.print('inserted em_event ' + ev.insert());
});</body><data>{"kind": "script", "purpose": "Creates a small set of test events through the OOB EvtMgmtCommons / em_event insert so rules, binding and incident creation can be verified. DRY RUN prints the payloads only.", "prereqs": "Sub-production only. Use a known CI name. Delete or close generated alerts after testing.", "rollback": "Generated events carry source \"DSB_TEST\"; close the resulting alerts and incidents."}</data><kind>implementation</kind><modifies_data>true</modifies_data><pattern display_value="ITOM Health: event management, AIOps and observability">27017c1f692149c79a16726ca19e8c2b</pattern><seq>1</seq><share_key/><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:22:06</sys_created_on><sys_id>87b5d6132ed24687b6d7719f9307e9e9</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:22:06</sys_updated_on><title>Test event generator (sub-prod only — creates events)</title></x_1577958_dsb_pattern_item></record_update>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><record_update table="x_1577958_dsb_pattern_item"><x_1577958_dsb_pattern_item action="INSERT_OR_UPDATE"><body>// DSB EVIDENCE hr.profile — READ ONLY.
// --- DSB helper prelude (read only; no personal information is printed) ---
var DSB_NOTES = [];
function _tbl(t){ return gs.tableExists(t); }
function _fieldOk(t, path){ var gr = new GlideRecord(t); var parts = path.split('.'); for (var i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) { if (!gr.isValidField(parts[i])) return false; if (i < parts.length - 1) { var ref = gr.getElement(parts[i]).getReferenceTable(); if (!ref) return false; gr = new GlideRecord(ref); } } return true; }
function _badField(t, q){ if (!q) return ''; var conds = String(q).split(/\^NQ|\^OR|\^/); for (var i = 0; i < conds.length; i++) { var m = conds[i].match(/^([a-z0-9_.]+)/); if (!m) continue; var f = m[1].replace(/\.$/, ''); if (f === 'sys_id') continue; if (!_fieldOk(t, f)) return f; } return ''; }
function count(t, q){ if (!_tbl(t)) return 'table not found'; var bad = _badField(t, q); if (bad) { DSB_NOTES.push(t + ': field not found ' + bad); return 'field not found: ' + bad; } var ga = new GlideAggregate(t); if (q) ga.addEncodedQuery(q); ga.addAggregate('COUNT'); ga.query(); return ga.next() ? parseInt(ga.getAggregate('COUNT'), 10) : 0; }
function groupCount(t, f, q, lim){ if (!_tbl(t)) return 'table not found'; var bad = _badField(t, q) || (_fieldOk(t, f) ? '' : f); if (bad) { DSB_NOTES.push(t + ': field not found ' + bad); return 'field not found: ' + bad; } var rows = []; var ga = new GlideAggregate(t); if (q) ga.addEncodedQuery(q); ga.addAggregate('COUNT'); ga.groupBy(f); ga.query(); var guard = 0; while (ga.next() && guard++ < 5000) rows.push([ga.getDisplayValue(f) || '(empty)', parseInt(ga.getAggregate('COUNT'), 10)]); rows.sort(function(a, b){ return b[1] - a[1]; }); var o = {}; rows.slice(0, lim || 50).forEach(function(r){ o[r[0]] = r[1]; }); if (rows.length > (lim || 50)) o['(other groups)'] = rows.length - (lim || 50); return o; }
function groupSet(t, f, q){ var o = {}; if (!_tbl(t) || !_fieldOk(t, f) || _badField(t, q)) return o; var ga = new GlideAggregate(t); if (q) ga.addEncodedQuery(q); ga.addAggregate('COUNT'); ga.groupBy(f); ga.query(); while (ga.next()) o[ga.getValue(f)] = parseInt(ga.getAggregate('COUNT'), 10); return o; }
function isNum(x){ return typeof x === 'number' && !isNaN(x); }
function diff(a, b){ return (isNum(a) && isNum(b)) ? a - b : 'n/a'; }
function pct(t, q, base){ var b = count(t, base); if (!isNum(b) || !b) return isNum(b) ? 0 : b; var c = count(t, base ? base + '^' + q : q); return isNum(c) ? Math.round(100 * c / b) : c; }
function hasField(t, f){ return _tbl(t) && _fieldOk(t, f); }
function dsbPrint(key, out){ if (DSB_NOTES.length) out.dsb_notes = DSB_NOTES; var LIM = 60000; var s = JSON.stringify(out, null, 1); if (s.length > LIM) s = JSON.stringify(out); var cut = [], loops = 0; while (s.length > LIM && loops++ < 60) { var bigK = null, bigL = 0; for (var k in out) { if (k === 'key' || k === 'dsb_truncated' || !out[k] || typeof out[k] !== 'object') continue; var l = JSON.stringify(out[k]).length; if (l > bigL) { bigL = l; bigK = k; } } if (!bigK) break; var v = out[bigK]; if (Object.prototype.toString.call(v) === '[object Array]' && v.length > 10) { out[bigK] = v.slice(0, Math.floor(v.length / 2)); cut.push(bigK + ' kept ' + out[bigK].length + ' of ' + v.length); } else { out[bigK] = 'omitted: ' + bigL + ' characters'; cut.push(bigK + ' omitted'); } out.dsb_truncated = cut; s = JSON.stringify(out); } gs.print('=== DSB-EVIDENCE ' + key + ' ===\n' + s); }
var MAX_ROWS = 5000;
var LAST90 = 'sys_created_onRELATIVEGT@dayofweek@ago@90';
var out = {key:'hr.profile'};
out.users_active = count('sys_user', 'active=true');
out.users_active_with_employee_number = count('sys_user', 'active=true^employee_numberISNOTEMPTY');
out.hr_profiles = count('sn_hr_core_profile');
out.hr_profiles_active_users = count('sn_hr_core_profile', 'user.active=true');
['employment_start_date','employment_type','work_country','position','location'].forEach(function(f){
  if (hasField('sn_hr_core_profile', f)) out['pct_profile_with_' + f] = pct('sn_hr_core_profile', f + 'ISNOTEMPTY', 'user.active=true');
});
out.user_sources = groupCount('sys_user', 'source', 'active=true');
out.hr_integration_apps = [];
var sa = new GlideRecord('sys_store_app'); sa.addEncodedQuery('nameLIKEWorkday^ORnameLIKESuccessFactors^ORnameLIKEOracle HCM^ORnameLIKEService Graph Connector'); sa.query();
while (sa.next()) out.hr_integration_apps.push(sa.getValue('name') + ' ' + sa.getValue('version'));
dsbPrint('hr.profile', out);</body><data>{"key": "hr.profile", "why": "Lifecycle events, criteria and routing depend on HR profile data", "unblocks": "HR integration design"}</data><kind>evidence_script</kind><modifies_data>false</modifies_data><pattern display_value="HR Service Delivery foundation and employee lifecycle">1a261fc057734397b446de21b49dcf22</pattern><seq>3</seq><share_key/><sys_created_by>emile.bennetts</sys_created_by><sys_created_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_created_on><sys_id>0319d4e651b248b498c944c9e79ae99e</sys_id><sys_mod_count>0</sys_mod_count><sys_updated_by>emile.bennetts</sys_updated_by><sys_updated_on>2026-09-27 17:21:48</sys_updated_on><title>HR profile coverage and data quality against active users</title></x_1577958_dsb_pattern_item></record_update>
